reviews.text: It all feels very bleak, and appalling, and horrifically absurd. The effect is absolutely superb.
reviews.author: Grant Watson

reviews.text: The Death of Stalin is its own firing squad armed with a specialized brand of heinous hilarity.
reviews.author: Don Shanahan

reviews.text: In the end, the humor fades away in favor of political machinations, but the film's killer gags are still numerable. Watching them delivered by expert performers is The Death of Stalin's primary pleasure.
reviews.author: Benedict Seal

reviews.text: I appear to be the rare early reviewer who didn’t dig it, so Iannucci die-hards can probably feel free to ignore me and anticipate.
reviews.author: Vadim Rizov

reviews.text: With caustic wit, Iannucci examines the humanity of his characters and the absurdity of their behavior with both passion and precision.
reviews.author: Brian T. Carney

reviews.text: Steve Buscemi is just a joy, as always.
reviews.author: Eve Tushnet

reviews.text: This is what great satires do: make us laugh while giving us glimpses of our own reality. The Death Of Stalin is a truly funny and absurdly smart film.
reviews.author: Daniel Howat

reviews.text: The brilliance of Iannucci's limber tonal shifts is that he can switch between them in an instant, keeping a sharp audience on edge, while never losing our investment in the film.
reviews.author: Brian Eggert

reviews.text: Politicians bumbling attempts to feign grief about Stalin's death while secretly delighted, functions as a running gag with a Python-ian flavor (heightened by Python emeritus Michael Palin in the cast) and thereby highlighting the absurdity of communism.
reviews.author: Mark Jackson

reviews.text: It's as mind-bendingly clever as it is completely silly.
reviews.author: Olly Richards

reviews.text: An audacious reimagining of history. Strong comic performances are highlighted in a film that is both frightening and funny at the same time.
reviews.author: Richard Crouse

reviews.text: The Death of Stalin is a fatally ill-conceived "black comedy" ... The film is not so much maliciously anticommunist as it is, above all, historically clueless.
reviews.author: David Walsh

reviews.text: Co-writer/director Iannucci handpicked these actors one at a time, and you can tell. Every actor fits the role like a tailored suit set to one ideal set of mannerisms. That's high-class skill.
reviews.author: Dan Buffa

reviews.text: Filled with political correctness, the dramatic points feel way more effective than the comedy. Absolutely gorgeous production design. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Victor Pineyro

reviews.text: 'This is just... wordplay,' one character exclaims, and while that doesn't come off as an intended auto-critique, it certainly could function as one at points.
reviews.author: Matt Cipolla

reviews.text: From backstabbing to assassination, pajamas, and concert recordings, it all seems so terribly trivial until it's all so terribly real. It's like Mean Girls, only with the fate of millions hanging in the balance.
reviews.author: Michael J. Casey

reviews.text: The Death of Stalin strikes a tricky tone, but it rings true. The events portrayed in the film happened 65 years ago, and that distance gives us the ability to laugh at this very dark chapter in this country's history.
reviews.author: Dan Tabor

reviews.text: A pretty good attempt at satirising the absurdities of end-game totalitarianism.
reviews.author: PJ Nabarro

reviews.text: Everything about this movie works, particularly depicting the dictator's inner circle as a frat house. Hilarious and unsettling.
reviews.author: Jorge Ignacio Castillo

reviews.text: It may be cringe-worthy at times, what with its propensity for showing the Soviet world of violence, torture, and bloodletting, but for those who like their parables to be challenging and salty, do not miss this exceptional film.
reviews.author: Jeff York

reviews.text: Armando Iannucci's new film is a scathing look at vile oppression, and a heap of fun as well.
reviews.author: Ard Vijn

reviews.text: It is a very funny comedy with an inspired cast that makes sure the political component will not dilute but neither monopolize the plot too much. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Mikel Zorrilla

reviews.text: In 1953, after 20 years of mass torture and killings, Soviet dictator Josef Stalin is at death's door, and good riddance.
reviews.author: Andiee Paviour

reviews.text: When the film ends, Iannucci seems to have invited us to rethink our relationship with the past and with present politicking. It's to his great credit that he does it all while making sides ache from laughing.
reviews.author: Andrew Kendall

reviews.text: Politics can sometimes be farcical, but they are serious business.
reviews.author: Dan Murrell

reviews.text: [It] is a clever, intelligent bit of political comedy, history played for laughs, that is a refreshingly change from the usual low humor comedies of recent years.
reviews.author: Cate Marquis

reviews.text: The brutal legacy of Stalin's regime is hardly the stuff of comedy [but] the script successfully negotiates a balance between jet-black comedy and horrific political drama.
reviews.author: Paula Fleri-Soler

reviews.text: The narrative is no slack and there's always something happening that keeps us alert and grinning from ear to ear.
reviews.author: Filipe Freitas

reviews.text: ...has a cleverness that withers into something more wearying.
reviews.author: Josh Larsen

reviews.text: This is black humor at its blackest and best. It shoots a taproot down to our deepest humanity, and it does so, ironically enough, by revealing the hellish sources of our own inhumanity.
reviews.author: Rick Levin

reviews.text: Already the premier political satirist of his era, Armando Iannucci pulls off his most impressive feat yet, turning the corpse-strewn power struggle that followed Joseph Stalin's sudden death into a lacerating and disturbingly relevant farce.
reviews.author: Daniel Barnes

reviews.text: I love political satire as much as anyone, but this film is insufferable with its back-slapping, elitist brand of supposed humor.
reviews.author: Louisa Moore

reviews.text: This film plays like a chess game where everyone wants to the throne, and only the most cunning will survive.
reviews.author: Alci Rengifo

reviews.text: Is there a more thrillingly inventive political satirist than Armando Iannucci? I doubt it.
reviews.author: Marlow Stern

reviews.text: Paralysed by fear, the right answer now the wrong answer; the Soviet Politburo sounds a lot like Twitter. Moving from panic to farce and biting one-liners, it's crammed with sharp performances (though Isaacs steals the show as Yorkshire's General Zhukov).
reviews.author: Sarah Cartland

reviews.text: Stalin serves up the cringe comedy of tyranny, where much of the humor lies in the way that the characters twist themselves into hopeless knots as they navigate a Soviet wonderland.
reviews.author: Andrew Wyatt

reviews.text: The Death of Stalin is one of the funniest, most absurdly dark and frighteningly relevant political satires I've ever had the pleasure of viewing.
reviews.author: Di Golding

reviews.text: Naturally, what happened behind the scenes after Stalin's death is murky and Iannucci approaches it coldly, making The Death of Stalin a satire as funny as it is dark. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Erick Ortiz

reviews.text: Iannucci is a born narrator for political comedy. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Javier Perez

reviews.text: The Death of Stalin has atypical humor and is lethal in its agile and sharp dialogue. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Erick Estrada

reviews.text: The perfect blend of black humor, The Death of Stalin has a very real message about the political world today.
reviews.author: Alan French

reviews.text: The Death of Stalin isn't about Stalin or what happened in 1953. Instead it's about the dark side of power and those who execute it. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Ernesto Diezmartinez

reviews.text: The Death of Stalin is rarely out-and-out hilarious, but the performances are top-notch and the writing is thoroughly witty, entertaining, and thought-provoking.
reviews.author: Jordan Blum

reviews.text: No joke is without a later payoff that mixes two or more things we've already laughed at together for another when you least expect it.
reviews.author: Jared Mobarak

reviews.text: The Death of Stalin is not only unexpected, but sharp, witty, and effectively spurious.
reviews.author: Robert Daniels

reviews.text: The Death of Stalin is a smart, quick-witted, and amusing comedy that pinpoints historical humor.
reviews.author: Annie Banks

reviews.text: In Iannucci's scathing satire, Stalin may have died but his punishingly inhuman legacy lives on.
reviews.author: Glenn Heath Jr.

reviews.text: ...as great as the ensemble is, the script is even better, easily making "The Death of Stalin" the best and funniest film of 2018 thus far.
reviews.author: Tom Santilli

reviews.text: The comedic timing is impeccable throughout, with no weak links.
reviews.author: Sarah Manvel

reviews.text: This queasy-funny mixture of alarm and panic with bleakness and horror underscores our desire for something nasty to happen in the halls of power.
reviews.author: A.S. Hamrah

reviews.text: This dark comedy includes scenes of kidnapping, torture, murder, and a kind of autopsy scene where Stalin's brain is removed from his skull, yet it remains, essentially a comedy. Comedy is serious business.
reviews.author: Robert Roten

reviews.text: If only the real world was, in fact, this tame in its political nonsense.
reviews.author: Christopher Campbell

reviews.text: ...in an era where villainy does in fact seem to keep prevailing, it's satisfying to watch them stumble and scramble for our amusement, if only for a while.
reviews.author: Joe Reid

reviews.text: Directed and co-written by Armando Iannucci (of In the Loop and Veep fame), the film incorporates farce, wordplay, sight gags, and satire into one hilarious Molotov cocktail.
reviews.author: Gary M. Kramer

reviews.text: The movie veers into slapstick territory at times, as Iannucci continually takes the spark of a true story and sets it on comic fire.
reviews.author: Kaleem Aftab

reviews.text: This film's grave, absurd, brilliant, and brutal historical context has a way of making the future look, if not hopeful, then at least familiar.
reviews.author: Sean Nelson

reviews.text: An incredibly funny film about a not-very-funny historical event.
reviews.author: Jim Schembri

reviews.text: a ruthless livewire comedy... It tempts and teases the rigidly ideological portions of our minds to step into the light and laugh.
reviews.author: John Serba

reviews.text: I only wish the (functional) realization was at the level of its (dazzling) performers. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Jordi Costa

reviews.text: Iannucci is at it again in his usual uproarious fashion, slinging gags like weapons and flinging devastating one-liners like Molotov cocktails.
reviews.author: Sarah Ward

reviews.text: It's a gamble that pays off handsomely-this is far and away the funniest film of the year so far.
reviews.author: Stephen Silver

reviews.text: Iannucci takes some historical liberties, da, and super-compresses all the post-Stalin angling for power... But the reverse-courses, doublespeak, and obfuscations are 1984-ish dystopia-politics at their bitter best.
reviews.author: Brian Gibson

reviews.text: Even if the motivations and events aren't always clear, the performances are often hilarious.
reviews.author: M. Faust

reviews.text: As I say, the movie has its moments. Just way fewer than expected and than many reviewers have promised.
reviews.author: Rick Kisonak

reviews.text: Even those turned off by the very thought of watching anything political at this point in time will find themselves caught up in this clever political farce.
reviews.author: Rebecca Murray

reviews.text: Comedy as dark as it gets, but a great cast and crew produce the laughs.
reviews.author: Ron Wilkinson

reviews.text: Nobody does mordant political vaudeville like Armando Iannucci. His touch is swift, sure and utterly poisonous.
reviews.author: Eleanor Ringel Cater

reviews.text: The film manages to be both scabrously funny and bone chilling as it nails Stalinism's absurdity and inhumanity.
reviews.author: Lynden Barber

reviews.text: Rousing slapstick political-comedy.
reviews.author: Dennis Schwartz

reviews.text: The funniest, smartest, most unforgiving comedy in years, and the best satiric film of the 2010s.
reviews.author: Tim Brayton

reviews.text: A world gone mad, shaped from fear, chaos, cronyism,toadyism and limitless corruption. It's not the present day.
reviews.author: Ray Pride

reviews.text: It may be savagely satirical but it's not very funny.
reviews.author: Susan Granger

reviews.text: A devastatingly funny dissection of power politics, stripping the mystique from it and those who worship it. Iannucci has done it again.
reviews.author: Sandra Hall

reviews.text: Comedy is not the obvious genre for dealing with a brutal autocrat who killed millions of his own people, but The Death of Stalin mostly works.
reviews.author: Alison Gillmor

reviews.text: Maybe the movie doesn't live up to the most lavish praise that's been heaped on it, but there's a certain grim pleasure to be had from seeing its knaves and fools stripped down to their essential, vulgar meanness...
reviews.author: Stuart Klawans

reviews.text: [We] laugh, and we get why we laugh, but everything about the humour is painfully uncomfortable.
reviews.author: Simon Foster

reviews.text: Although it would be facile to compare modern politics to the horrors of Stalin's purge, there is something queasily resonant about a movie depicting a country on the verge of a nervous breakdown.
reviews.author: Rob Thomas

reviews.text: [Steve] Buscemi is just brilliant as pragmatic Khrushchev.
reviews.author: Philip Martin

reviews.text: The Death of Stalin is signature Iannucci - absurd set-ups leading to even more outrageous ends via the spitefully delicious cadence of his dialogue.
reviews.author: Wenlei Ma

reviews.text: Iannucci's fondness for chat does overwhelm certain scenes, but this is still ruthlessly funny, if not quite knockabout hilarious, which makes you wonder if something more subversive and satirical is going on.
reviews.author: David 'Mad Dog' Bradley

reviews.text: In The Death of Stalin, you will find a political comedy so dark, the punchlines are all but blacked out. So be warned: while there is much to admire here, you may find little to be amused by.
reviews.author: Leigh Paatsch

reviews.text: "Buscemi leads the cast valiantly in what are sharp comedic performances all around, guided by Iannucci's most savage political satire to date."
reviews.author: Molly Laich

reviews.text: Enormously witty dialogue ... the finest of ensembles, headed by Steve Buscemi, in the performance his entire career has been leading to ... something of a satirical masterpiece, and a bloody good history lesson to boot!
reviews.author: CJ Johnson

reviews.text: The Death of Stalin overcomes several obstacles to prove that it is both funny and cinematic.
reviews.author: Damien Straker

reviews.text: Tales of the venal, the selfish, and the desperate, lurking--when not preening--in the halls of power.
reviews.author: Peter Canavese

reviews.text: Kind of like Veep with a hammer and sickle, smart, tart and daftly topical.
reviews.author: Steve Persall

reviews.text: [Armando] Iannucci goes out of his way to really push the envelope to create some super memorable caricatures from living memory.
reviews.author: Amelia Navascues

reviews.text: If satire is dying, then The Death of Stalin, the latest film from Scottish writer-director Armando Iannucci, is a defibrillator, shocking the genre back to life.
reviews.author: Thaddeus McCollum

reviews.text: Death is the liveliest movie about brutal oppression I've seen in a while (since 1995's Underground, anyway); it's funny as hell - then suddenly chilling - and it's more audacious than just about anything else playing now.
reviews.author: Steve Murray

reviews.text: The Death of Stalin is obviously a farce, in the best sense; the primary aim is never verisimilitude. The film shares something of the attitude and atmosphere that pervades a work like Dario Fo's.
reviews.author: Anwen Crawford

reviews.text: The Death of Stalin manages to capture and contain a multitude of perspectives and players, both large and small, in its frames, while never losing sight of the very serious historic notes.
reviews.author: tt stern-enzi

reviews.text: Don't believe the hype. A far more intriguing, follow the money power struggle off screen instead, pitting corporate interests against the mass popular discontent of the downwardly mobile US population in progress. In other words, who funded your movie.
reviews.author: Prairie Miller

reviews.text: "Veep" creator Armando Iannucci and his remarkably comedic cast produce some very big laughs, particularly in the early going.
reviews.author: John Urbancich

reviews.text: Iannucci made the bravura decision to make a factual film of that event dressed in the black robe of English satire at its darkest. Surely, there was no other intelligent way to bring the story to an audience 75 years after the event.
reviews.author: Andrew L. Urban

reviews.text: If you like your movies black, thought provoking and hilariously funny, you will adore this audacious, irreverent satire that delves deep into the bowels of Russian politics and picks off scabs.
reviews.author: Louise Keller

reviews.text: "The Death of Stalin" is a deep farce, but it is rooted in enough political reality that it hardly feels sensationalized. And given the current state of politics, it's as on-point as a breaking news alert.
reviews.author: Adam Graham

reviews.text: While much of this is certainly hilarious, there are also scenes that drag.
reviews.author: David Stratton

reviews.text: The performances from Buscemi and Tambor have to be rated for their comic timing more than for historical nuance, and of the group, Beale stands out the most as he feels the walls of conspiracy closing in.
reviews.author: Josh Terry

reviews.text: It's cutting-edge political satire worthy of Russian dramatists Gogol or Bulgakov - farcical and frightening. Throat-cutting edge, you might say.
reviews.author: Barry Paris

reviews.text: A timely satire for those moviegoers who are fine with taking the film at face value - as a silly ribbing of government corruption - and those who find comfort in comparing the nonsense on screen to America's own political reality show.
reviews.author: Kiko Martinez

reviews.text: Iannucci hits these Communists so hard, so often you'll wish he'd let up a little on these murderous comrades.
reviews.author: Christian Toto

reviews.text: ...offers the chance to observe a world ruled by absurdity from a safe distance...
reviews.author: Sarah Boslaugh

reviews.text: Once again, if you know how Iannucci works, you can expect Stalin to be as hilariously foul-mouthed as his previous works.
reviews.author: Craig D. Lindsey

reviews.text: I can't think of another movie exactly like The Death of Stalin, which is part of the reason this movie feels so unsettlingly original.
reviews.author: Robert Denerstein

reviews.text: The Death of Stalin is actually a lot like Veep, except with gulags and executions.
reviews.author: Chris Vognar

reviews.text: If the mixture of brutality and wackiness doesn't always gel, Iannucci earns points for audacity alone. Any movie that's been banned in Putin's Russia is worth seeing,
reviews.author: Frank Swietek

reviews.text: Like the '60s British political comedies it resembles, The Death of Stalin may be too clever, too mordant. But it does have tang, Tom Stoppard-like wordplay and some big and surprising laughs.
reviews.author: Richard von Busack

reviews.text: Director and co-writer Armando Iannucci puts it all on black (comedy), betting that the vast discrepancy between great power and small souls will make you laugh at the absurdity of it all - or at least not scream in horror.
reviews.author: Matthew Lickona

reviews.text: "The Death of Stalin" should please moviegoers who appreciate humor that's significantly more sophisticated than we've become accustomed to encountering on the big screen these days.
reviews.author: Calvin Wilson

reviews.text: "The Death of Stalin" makes real-life horrors the source of hilarity - and it is hilarious - while never making light of the insanity that inspired it.
reviews.author: Bill Goodykoontz

reviews.text: For Iannucci, who loves to mock the craven, unprincipled pursuit of power, the scenario is an antic delight and plays to his talent for hectic plot turns and (pardon the expression) rapid-fire dialogue.
reviews.author: Gary Thompson

reviews.text: What better material to employ so many fine comic actors, masters all of the anxious flutter, the pained smirk and the deftly parried bon mot? You don't need to know a lot about mid-century Soviet politics to thoroughly enjoy this film
reviews.author: Al Hoff

reviews.text: Blend The West Wing with Fawlty Towers and add a smidge of Dr. Strangelove, and you're getting close to the feel of The Death of Stalin.
reviews.author: Mike Scott

reviews.text: The hint that he and the writers are dropping is that if we can guffaw at these monsters, we can deal with anything. See The Death of Stalin and face the future unafraid.
reviews.author: Kelly Vance

reviews.text: They sit around kibitzing and laughing, with one eye on Stalin to ensure that they haven't crossed some line that will have them and their families shot at dawn.
reviews.author: Jay Stone

reviews.text: Labors inside the sort of buffoonery that Burn After Reading achieved with much more cohesive performances and comic richness.
reviews.author: Matt Pais

reviews.text: Armando Iannucci explores how people in lofty offices don't have to be evil geniuses to cause irreparable harm...Iannucci skillfully manages to poke fun at pettiness while never losing track of how horrific Soviet purges were.
reviews.author: Dan Lybarger

reviews.text: Iannucci did not intend The Death of Stalin to be a direct commentary on the Trump presidency, and it should not be taken as one. But as they say: First time tragedy, second time farce.
reviews.author: Christopher Orr

reviews.text: This isn't just a picture about the state of the Soviet Union in March 1953; it's very much about today.
reviews.author: Al Alexander

reviews.text: The Death of Stalin is Iannucci's most complex and almost nihilistic rendering of what politics is:
reviews.author: Emily St. James

reviews.text: In The Death of Stalin, Iannucci brings his sharp ear for political doublespeak and workplace absurdity to the days after the demise of the notorious Soviet dictator...It's Iannucci's best work yet, although it might not be his funniest.
reviews.author: Noah Gittell

reviews.text: Iannucci has taken a gamble with this movie, and that gamble has paid off handsomely. A tale of mortal sins as well as venial ones, The Death of Stalin adds modern urgency to his comic storytelling trademarks.
reviews.author: Andy Crump

reviews.text: From start to finish, director/co-writer Armando Iannucci (creator of HBO's brilliant Veep) delivers an audacious and insightful and ridiculous and hilarious send-up that reminded me of the classic Monty Python films of the 1970s and 1980s.
reviews.author: Richard Roeper

reviews.text: ... apart from Iannucci's own In The Loop, there's not much in recent English language cinema to even compare it to. Very recommended.
reviews.author: Graeme Tuckett

reviews.text: The actors give top-rate, impressively in-character performances.
reviews.author: Anita Katz

reviews.text: There's a universality to the humor that will reach even those with only a vague knowledge of who Stalin was.
reviews.author: James Berardinelli

reviews.text: The central conceit of The Death of Stalin is that what is funny is not always just funny. In this sense, the film is closer in spirit to Dr. Strangelove than, say Mel Brooks's The Producers.
reviews.author: Peter Rainer

reviews.text: Amusing but broad, Marxism meets Mark Bros. take on last days of dictator from Veep's Armando Ianucci.
reviews.author: James Verniere

reviews.text: 'The Death of Stalin' may sound daunting, but poking at a dead dictator hasn't been this much fun since the days of Chaplin and the Marx Brothers.
reviews.author: Jeffrey M. Anderson

reviews.text: An often interminable misfire...
reviews.author: David Nusair

reviews.text: Comes close to perfectly balancing comedy and savagery.
reviews.author: Robert Horton

reviews.text: There is something revelatory about transporting the bureaucratic machinations featured in Iannucci's previous work to the gulag archipelago that was Soviet Russia.
reviews.author: Sonny Bunch

reviews.text: The film is ruthless in its dissection of these people...
reviews.author: Mark Dujsik

reviews.text: Armando Iannucci's satire is blisteringly on point and delightfully scathing
reviews.author: Robert Kojder

reviews.text: This is satirical history that invites prophecy - imagine a future Trump Administration version.
reviews.author: Bruce DeMara

reviews.text: It's some of the darkest humor you'll see on the big screen this year.
reviews.author: Charles Ealy

reviews.text: Iannucci may have turned Nury's somber novel into something of a goof, but he also takes a more complex view of Beria...Death of Stalin is a priceless political satir but what's really impressive is how hard it tries to fit Beria's story into the puzzle.
reviews.author: J. R. Jones

reviews.text: If it's a romp, then it's a romp that does what anything on this topic must do: leave audiences a little rattled, with a hint of ashes in the mouth.
reviews.author: Michael Phillips

reviews.text: Vladimir Putin's Ministry of Culture ministry has banned "The Death of Stalin" from being shown in Russia. There can be no greater praise.
reviews.author: Ty Burr

reviews.text: The Soviet Union may be no more, but we can still laugh about the bad old days.
reviews.author: Chris Knight

reviews.text: If you thought Armando Iannucci's takes on modern British and American politics were entertaining, just wait till you get a load of this hilarious and horrifying spin on a key moment in Russian history.
reviews.author: James Croot

reviews.text: Veep creator Armando Iannucci directs this bumbling display with consistently biting wit that doesn't venture too far into farce to be taken credibly.
reviews.author: Leigh Monson

reviews.text: "The Death of Stalin" is a weird sort of hilarious, in that you easily might not laugh for minutes at a time. Instead of one big pie in the face, doled out at intervals, the movie presents an unending series of comic jabs ...
reviews.author: Mick LaSalle

reviews.text: The Death of Stalin never mocks historical horrors. Instead, the broadness, the outrageousness, with which it dramatizes the banality of evil - and bureaucracy, too - is what makes it so very chilling.
reviews.author: Kimberley Jones

reviews.text: Sight gags and slapstick erupt from a pervasive atmosphere of dread and terror.
reviews.author: Christopher Kompanek

reviews.text: It is a propitious material for the most incisive humor, for its sociopolitical core. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Ignacio Navarro

reviews.text: While its shtick runs out a bit sooner than its runtime does, The Death of Stalin milks the sick irony of its setting for all it's worth.
reviews.author: Brian Thompson

reviews.text: Contributing to the theatre-of-the-absurdism, there are no phony accents. Which means we get Steve Buscemi as Nikita Khrushchev sounding exactly like Steve Buscemi. It suggests craven self-interest is universal and not just a "Russian thing."
reviews.author: Jim Slotek

reviews.text: ...the blackest of humor. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Alberto Luchini

reviews.text: Historically speaking, you might say the dossier has been sexed up but I totally wallowed in the thing like a pig in muck...
reviews.author: Paul Casserly

reviews.text: It's funny; ten times funnier, by my reckoning, than it has any right to be, and more riddled with risk than anything that Iannucci has done before, because it dares to meet outrage with outrage.
reviews.author: Anthony Lane

reviews.text: Satire or farce, it misses the mark showing murderous, heartless brutes as akin to Keystone Kops. If they want to use real people and real names and real events, tell the real story. Chaplin changed everything but you knew it was Hitler. That's farce
reviews.author: Tony Medley

reviews.text: ... a hilarious political satire that uses its titular event as the launching pad for a revisionist romp with subtle contemporary resonance.
reviews.author: Todd Jorgenson

reviews.text: Language, violence in amazing, absurd historical comedy.
reviews.author: Michael Ordoña

reviews.text: High-stakes politics, small-minded men: It's a sweet spot for filmmaker Armando Iannucci.
reviews.author: John Anderson

reviews.text: When it comes to contemporary crafters of political satire, Armando Iannucci exists in an exalted realm all his own.
reviews.author: Robert Levin

reviews.text: It's a rich ensemble with varying accents, from Cockney to American, and uniform comic brilliance, including Michael Palin as Molotov, Jeffrey Tambor as Malenkov and Jason Isaacs as Zhukov.
reviews.author: Jake Coyle

reviews.text: In "The Death of Stalin," a rambling, messy, fascinating film, the laughs come with a poisonous sting.
reviews.author: Jordan Ruimy

reviews.text: It never asks us to laugh at cruelty; it does make us laugh at the absurd pettiness and ultimate small-mindedness of the men perpetrating that cruelty. And Iannucci is a superb ringmaster.
reviews.author: Glenn Kenny

reviews.text: The Death of Stalin is a breath of fresh air and a genuinely great screen comedy. Iannucci conducts the proceedings like the conductor of a great orchestra with an array of virtuosos at his command.
reviews.author: Leonard Maltin

reviews.text: A breathtakingly dark comedy of errors with petty sniping and profane insults, cheerfully mining laughs from ghastly true events.
reviews.author: Eric D. Snider

reviews.text: Though The Death of Stalin is a one-joke movie about how plotting and pandemonium invariably pour into a leadership vacuum, it's a deadly serious joke that we'd do well to attend to.
reviews.author: Ella Taylor

reviews.text: The script feels like a great writers-room comedy, where only the leanest and meanest bits stay, and the most startling and intriguing ideas persist.
reviews.author: Blake Goble

reviews.text: The chaos is darkly hilarious...
reviews.author: Tim Appelo

reviews.text: Steve Buscemi, Simon Russell Beale, Michael Palin, Jeffrey Tambor and Jason Isaacs create a formidable and selfless comedic quintet, while Iannucci's unyielding script and direction constantly stirs, twists and builds without ever overwhelming.
reviews.author: Gregory Wakeman

reviews.text: Even played for comedy, the conditions surrounding, the characters affected by, and the succession struggle that followed Stalin's death are so rich in human drama as to be potentially Shakespearean.
reviews.author: J. Hoberman

reviews.text: As long as The Death of Stalin is sticking it to the hypocrites in the Kremlin-mocking their vanity, pride, and other deadly sins-it's got the righteous riotousness of its creator's best work.
reviews.author: Adam Nayman

reviews.text: It isn't history but free-range fiction, a venomous farce containing nuggets of fact, and if its subjects bear any resemblance to present-day dictators and authoritarian mugs or thugs around the world, then the movie has hit its archetypal target.
reviews.author: Joe Morgenstern

reviews.text: a deft achievement, the telling of a treacherous historical event with the comedic chaos of the Marx Brothers and abrupt physical farce of the Three Stooges.
reviews.author: Laura Clifford

reviews.text: "The Death of Stalin" is by turns entertaining and unsettling, with laughs that morph into gasps and uneasy gasps that erupt into queasy, choking laughs.
reviews.author: Manohla Dargis

reviews.text: If anyone has a gift for ferreting out the "petty" in petty tyranny, it's Veep creator Armando Iannucci.
reviews.author: Leah Greenblatt

reviews.text: Thankfully, "Stalin" doesn't tucker out completely, and Iannucci's vision stretches without snapping, managing to make a biting but silly comedy out of political anxiety behind the Iron Curtain.
reviews.author: Brian Orndorf

reviews.text: This is a comedy of terrors that creates laughs but doesn't let you forget that Stalin and his coterie caused the deaths of untold numbers of Soviet citizens.
reviews.author: Kenneth Turan

reviews.text: As Stanley Kubrick did with Dr. Strangelove, Iannucci has built a satire not by twisting the truth but by nudging reality just a few inches further in the direction it was already going.
reviews.author: Bilge Ebiri

reviews.text: The Death of Stalin brings Iannucci's love for political satire to a period in history that nobody could have expected.
reviews.author: Danielle Solzman

reviews.text: It takes some time to adjust to the mix of silly, peevish bureaucrats and the serious atrocities they inflict. But that's the beauty of the thing.
reviews.author: David Edelstein

reviews.text: Not since Ernst Lubitsch's To Be or Not to Be has there been a movie satire as audacious as Armando Iannucci's The Death of Stalin.
reviews.author: Kevin Lally

reviews.text: Armando Iannucci's hilarious, profane satire about politburos pole-positioning for power could not be more timely. It's the funniest, fiercest comedy of the year.
reviews.author: Peter Travers

reviews.text: I admired its daring and its ambition, but though it's well worth your time, it doesn't entirely come off.
reviews.author: Kyle Smith

reviews.text: There's an irony here: In the interest of dramatic expediency, Iannucci has made the power players of The Death Of Stalin look more competent and more decisive than their real counterparts.
reviews.author: Ignatiy Vishnevetsky

reviews.text: We can expect great work from the director [Armando Iannucci] in his major specialty: the ingenious insult. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Yago García

reviews.text: It is still a fascinating, engaging, and tongue-in-cheek look at one of the most chaotic of political times and the final moments of one of the most ruthless dictators the world has ever known.
reviews.author: Andrew Pollard

reviews.text: ...pedestrian pulling humor. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Jordi Batlle Caminal

reviews.text: I enjoyed this so much that I screened it twice, back-to-back.
reviews.author: Adrian Mack

reviews.text: Armando Iannucci satirizes the manner in which political power is accorded to those who can mask cutthroat ambition behind an outward projection of bland inoffensiveness.
reviews.author: Jake Cole

reviews.text: There's much to satirize about the struggle for power in the Kremlin after Stalin's death, but this juvenile, overly-broad comedy does not rise to the level of parody.
reviews.author: Harvey S. Karten

reviews.text: This goofy cinematic vantage on the petty jealousies, backstabbing, and political maneuvering of Russia's Central Committee gives its audience a not so unrealistic sense of how politicians operate regardless of their country of origin.
reviews.author: Cole Smithey

reviews.text: What luck we've had that Armando Iannucci was in charge of bringing this book to the screen. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Paula Arantzazu Ruiz

reviews.text: "The Death of Stalin" is a wickedly funny, pointedly scathing satire of corrupt power run amok.
reviews.author: Joe Bendel

reviews.text: ...some genuinely hilarious set ups and a nice mixture of farce and other styles of comedy.
reviews.author: Julian Wood

reviews.text: There's real horror in it too at times...It's a risk, where it could've been guilty of overreaching, but there's a chaotic tone here established into which it all fits quite snugly.
reviews.author: Ed Williamson

reviews.text: Kudos are deserved everywhere for a well-written, beautifully played and offbeat piece of re-imagined history that's always funny despite humour sometimes stemming from a distinct sense of unease.
reviews.author: David Aldridge

reviews.text: A little gem of black humor and historical revision. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Aurélie Dupire

reviews.text: A dark, hilarious tour de force.
reviews.author: Chris Evangelista

reviews.text: This dark and absurdist comedy is hugely enjoyable; but when it comes to authoritarian regimes, some more tragedy might have felt more affecting.
reviews.author: Roe McDermott

reviews.text: The Death of Staling feels like a play, but doesn't feel like watching one. It feels like being in one, and it's a raucous, hilarious, hard-hitting play at that.
reviews.author: Siddhant Adlakha

reviews.text: A film that rides the line between irreverence and farce without trivialising the plight of the victims.
reviews.author: Ed Whitfield

reviews.text: Playing it straight is the secret. Turn down the volume and the picture would resemble any costume drama. Crank it back up again and the air becomes saltier than the Seregovo mine.
reviews.author: Ryan Gilbey

reviews.text: Audacious, outrageous, bleakly funny. Not since Charlie Chaplin sent up Hitler and invited us to laugh at terrible reality has there been a movie like this.
reviews.author: MaryAnn Johanson

reviews.text: Jeffrey Tambor is perfect as the lugubrious Malenkov, and Beale oozes malice as Stalin's sadistic henchman Beria. And what a masterstroke it was to cast Steve Buscemi as Khrushchev.
reviews.author: Paul Whitington

reviews.text: An impressive-looking and well-acted production that allows Jason Isaacs, as Field Marshal Zhukov, to show off his little-known talent for comedy, and which should see the genuinely brilliant Beale land a generous hatful of award nominations.
reviews.author: Matthew Bond

reviews.text: Taken on its own terms, the movie is so enjoyable that niggles can easily be set aside. Above all, it's rich in good performances.
reviews.author: Edward Porter

reviews.text: A comprehensive rebuttal to those who say comedy cannot be fashioned from the most miserable circumstance.
reviews.author: Donald Clarke

reviews.text: In a rather weak year for big screen comedy, The Death of Stalin can easily stake a claim as the year's funniest film.
reviews.author: Alistair Ryder

reviews.text: Just because The Death of Stalin is not Iannucci's funniest or most consistent work does not mean it's a total letdown.
reviews.author: Tomas Trussow

reviews.text: A frighteningly funny satire that finds humour in historical horror. Watch and feel better about the world.
reviews.author: Jordan Farley

reviews.text: The tone ends up being oddly serious, the comedy bleak rather than black, and the final product is somehow both more sombre and less caustic than Iannucci's sharpest, silliest work.
reviews.author: Simran Hans

reviews.text: Actual quantities of laughter are diluted by the difficult satiric point, but the acting and the farce's whirring clockwork occupy you anyway.
reviews.author: Nick Hasted

reviews.text: The film is uproariously funny but painfully close to the bone in a world where once again the lunatics have taken over the asylum.
reviews.author: Lisa Mullen

reviews.text: For all his dream-team cast and assured direction, despite capturing the laughable sycophancy of the apparatchik the film isn't that funny.
reviews.author: Matthew Norman

reviews.text: The film is savagely, often uproariously, comic but the laughter freezes on your lips as you question if something this horrible can ever be truly funny.
reviews.author: Allan Hunter

reviews.text: The Death of Stalin transforms the murky and tricky historical period surrounding the death of Joseph Stalin in March 1953 into a punchy, raucous, savagely smart comedy.
reviews.author: Kevin Maher

reviews.text: It makes Stalin and his gang look as absurd as they were abominable, which can't be a bad thing.
reviews.author: Brian Viner

reviews.text: Comedy of the year by a country mile.
reviews.author: Jamie East

reviews.text: Generally, though, The Death of Stalin is an entertaining and often funny film, the tone of which will be familiar, if not wholly so, to fans of Iannucci's excellent previous work.
reviews.author: Martin Roberts

reviews.text: This is not Iannucci's best work, but as Iannucci on a bad day is better than most on a good day, and there are brilliant moments, and you just can't argue with Simon Russell Beale -- in anything -- it's not nearly two hours wasted.
reviews.author: Deborah Ross

reviews.text: Witty and scarily pertinent to almost any organisation, The Death Of Stalin is so brilliant it's a privilege to watch it.
reviews.author: Larushka Ivan-Zadeh

reviews.text: Darker and more violent than Iannucci's previous work, this is a brilliantly acted and very funny black comedy underscored with a jolt of genuine horror.
reviews.author: Matthew Turner

reviews.text: Depending on your point of view, The Death of Stalin is either a sly, wintry satire on Armando Iannucci's usual theme of squawking political idiocy, or an insidious attempt to destabilise the Russian establishment with relentless dagger-blows.
reviews.author: Tim Robey

reviews.text: Iannucci's version of events may be well researched but it still gives us a very British, very witty but facetious version of a dark story which might have been better told by an insider.
reviews.author: Geoffrey Macnab

reviews.text: ... Armando Iannucci's passable screwball comedy which might aspire to satire but actually isn't so.
reviews.author: Paddy Kehoe

reviews.text: An audacious comedy of horrors, the film has the feel of a bad dream you find yourself not wanting to wake up from.
reviews.author: Danny Leigh

reviews.text: A riotous farce of doublespeak and plotting laced with moments of bitumen-black horror.
reviews.author: Philip De Semlyen

reviews.text: Make sure you pay your respects to the funniest film of 2017, as Monty Python meets TV's The Thick of It in this outrageous and brilliant historical satirical farce.
reviews.author: Chris Hunneysett

reviews.text: Taken strictly as a workout in elastic ensemble performance and rapid-fire verbal pugilism, The Death of Stalin is consistently entertaining. But enjoying Iannucci's film means depoliticizing the source material.
reviews.author: Steve Macfarlane

reviews.text: Mixes hard shocks and big laughs to often dazzling effect.
reviews.author: David Jenkins

reviews.text: A film as riotously funny as it is alarmingly pertinent.
reviews.author: Emma Simmonds

reviews.text: This is classic comedy gold, in many ways reminiscent of the old Monty Python show sketches skewering politicians, but with a slightly more serious spin.
reviews.author: April Wolfe

reviews.text: Armando Iannucci pulls off a balancing act that's more remarkable the more you think about it: this is a movie that's both mercilessly grim and uproariously funny.
reviews.author: Jason Bailey

reviews.text: Surreal, intriguing and strangely affecting, The Death of Stalin is simultaneously familiar and totally different to anything Armando Iannucci has done before.
reviews.author: Benjamin Rabinovich

reviews.text: The Death of Stalin is full of pithy one-liners and cringe-inducing power struggles laced with black humor.
reviews.author: Richard Porton

reviews.text: [Armando] Iannucci has never turned in a film that looks this ravishing, which serves as an interesting juxtaposition with all the top-shelf cruelty on display.
reviews.author: Scott Wampler

reviews.text: Heaps of praise will be deservedly lumped onto the core cast members, but some of the movie's sharpest moments come from the supporting cast.
reviews.author: Matt Shiverdecker

reviews.text: The Death of Stalin is a scathingly funny satire about power-mad nerds and bumbling bureaucrats that could only come from Armando Iannucci.
reviews.author: Sarah Marrs

reviews.text: This may be Iannucci's weakest-written film, but it's by far his best-directed one.
reviews.author: Dan Schindel

reviews.text: For those who've enjoyed Armando Iannucci's latter day career as the driving force behind The Thick Of It and Veep, The Death Of Stalin reassuringly offers more of the same.
reviews.author: Michael Bonner

reviews.text: As perfectly conducted as the orchestra performances that open and close the film, The Death Of Stalin zips along merrily as alliances are formed, plots are hatched and lives are destroyed.
reviews.author: Norman Wilner

reviews.text: The Death of Stalin is Iannucci's most complex and almost nihilistic rendering of what politics is: A team of bumbling and weak-minded people who lack any real conviction other than a desire for power and position.
reviews.author: Alissa Wilkinson

reviews.text: Iannucci masterfully blends dark humour about an authoritarian regime and farcical comedy performed with perfect timing.
reviews.author: Caryn James

reviews.text: Its application of [Iannucci's] signature barbed comic voice to such grim history (executions are a constant source of gallows humor) packs its own punch.
reviews.author: A.A. Dowd

reviews.text: A delicious black comedy ...
reviews.author: Sara Stewart

reviews.text: It will more than satisfy Iannucci's fans at arthouses; here's hoping we don't have to wait another eight years to see the director's next film.
reviews.author: John DeFore

reviews.text: The Death of Stalin marks the first instance in which Iannucci has applied his style to real-life figures, and it's as though he has crafted a historical foundation for the rest of his work.
reviews.author: Eric Kohn

reviews.text: Master satirist Armando Iannucci's new film is ostensibly a comedy, but the laughs don't come easy and the jokes are often laced with malice and paranoia.
reviews.author: Tim Grierson

reviews.text: There is one thing that power can't stand, and that is to be mocked: The social importance of this topical romp should not be underestimated.
reviews.author: Kate Taylor

reviews.text: An occasionally funny, often straight-faced film about a cruel leader's cronies and how self-interest doesn't stall for death.
reviews.author: Vikram Murthi

reviews.text: A raunchy, hilarious history lesson.
reviews.author: Chris Bumbray

reviews.text: Although the laughs don't come as frequently as In the Loop or Veep, The Death of Stalin is still consistently funny and delightfully mean-spirited.
reviews.author: Matt Goldberg

reviews.text: Iannucci's brand of political satire is applied to one of the darkest chapters in modern history, with sensational results.
reviews.author: Nick De Semlyen

reviews.text: n our age of real life self-mocking, opinionated hogwash, the surrealist/satirist Iannucci has, with The Death of Stalin, once again nailed it.
reviews.author: Daniel Goodwin

reviews.text: Armando Iannucci, always a sharp observer of the complex motivations that fuel political behavior, doesn't miss a beat.
reviews.author: Kevin Jagernauth

reviews.text: As lurid as dark comedies go, The Death of Stalin is one of the year's most outrageously fun and provocative films.
reviews.author: Jason Gorber

reviews.text: If only the end result were as funny as the idea that anyone would undertake a film about the turmoil surrounding the Soviet despot's demise.
reviews.author: Peter Debruge

reviews.text: The Death Of Stalin is superbly cast, and acted with icy and ruthless force by an A-list lineup. There are no weak links. Each has a plum role; each squeezes every gorgeous horrible drop.
reviews.author: Peter Bradshaw

synopsis: When tyrannical dictator Joseph Stalin dies in 1953, his parasitic cronies square off in a frantic power struggle to become the next Soviet leader. Among the contenders are the dweebish Georgy Malenkov, the wily Nikita Khrushchev and Lavrenti Beria -- the sadistic secret police chief. As they bumble, brawl and back-stab their way to the top, the question remains -- just who is running the government?
